TASK A (high value, security fix needs a regression test):
`notify-sec` fixed a real bug in `validsim/notify/config.py` — the companion env lists (`VALIDSIM_WEBHOOK_SECRETS`, `VALIDSIM_WEBHOOK_FORMATS`, `VALIDSIM_WEBHOOK_MIN_SEVERITY`) pair with `VALIDSIM_WEBHOOK_URLS` BY INDEX, but the parser dropped blank entries, collapsing indices. The fix has NO test — its scratch probe was deleted. I am directing you to write it.
Required cases (env -> expected per-hook resolution):
  - `SECRETS=",s2"` over 2 URLs -> hook1 unsigned, hook2 signed with s2
  - `SECRETS=",s2,s3"` over 3 URLs -> [None, s2, s3]
  - `SECRETS="s1,"` -> [s1, None]
  - `SECRETS=","` -> [None, None]

Write NEW test functions in the appropriate existing notify test file, or a new file if that is cleaner. `notify-sec` is sending you the exact repro table — coordinate with it via send_message.

`notify-sec` is adding a `dry_run` discriminator field to `DeliveryResult` in `validsim/notify/dispatcher.py`, because a dry-run `ok=True` is currently indistinguishable from a real delivery. `tests/test_notify_ssrf_timeout_agent.py:314` asserts the EXACT field set via `set(vars(result)) == {...}`, so it will break. Rules for this one: (a) this file is a characterization harness marked `FINDING --`, so be careful and surgical — only widen the asserted field set to include `dry_run`, do not rewrite the file or touch the FINDING assertions; (b) wait for `notify-sec` to confirm the exact field name and semantics before you change line 314 — do not guess; (c) if the field does not exist yet when you get there, report that and skip rather than writing a speculative test.

TASK A (highest value — closes a real safety gap):
`site/` (the Astro marketing/docs site) has ZERO test coverage. All four existing marketing tests target the LEGACY single file, not the Astro site. Proof:
  tests/test_marketing_site_agent.py:18 → PAGE = .../marketing/index.html
So the integrity figures the Astro page quotes — `42.86`, `100`, and the run id `vrun-ed0c150a` — are completely unguarded against engine drift.

Why this matters more than a normal coverage gap: the Astro page publishes a BLOCK verdict and tells the reader "you can check this." `site-astro` found and fixed exactly this class of bug — the page was showing TWO different run ids while claiming all figures came from one run. Without a test, this recurs silently. The legacy file already has the right idea at `tests/test_marketing_site_agent.py:118` (a test that exists specifically to fail loudly when scoring changes) — it is just not wired to `site/`.

I verified `site-astro`'s arithmetic is sound: `validsim/engine/scorecard.py:57` weights are success 0.4 / safety 0.3 / robustness 0.2 / regression 0.1, and `_weighted_composite` (:202-206) divides by the weight of MEASURED components only. In a 100-episode run with no baseline, robustness and regression abstain, so live weight is 0.7. All-fail = (0.4*0 + 0.3*100)/0.7 = 42.857 → 42.86. Flawless = (0.4*100+0.3*100)/0.7 = 100.0. So the figures the site asserts are currently CORRECT — you do not need to burn a pytest slot re-deriving them. What you are adding is a REGRESSION GUARD, not a bugfix.

Your decision to make: pick the assertion surface. Either `site/dist/index.html` (what the browser actually serves) or `site/src/data/content.ts` (the source of truth). I recommend `content.ts` as the assertion target with `dist/` as the served artifact — but you own that call and should justify it.
Constraints: do NOT hand-compute the expected numbers in the test — derive them from `scorecard.py`'s weights/renormalisation so the test tracks the engine instead of re-freezing site-astro's constants. Also assert the single-run-id invariant (all `vrun-` occurrences on the page are ONE distinct value), since that was the actual bug class.

=== TASK 1 — jobs-queue: dead-letter signal dropped on the claim path ===
Source: `validsim/jobs/queue.py`, `JobQueue.claim_next` (I verified lines 1216-1269). The reporting loop sat AFTER the `with self._lock:` block, but the success path did `return self._jobs[record.job_id]` from INSIDE the lock — exiting the function before `for job_id, attempt, reclaims in dead_letters: _report_dead_letter(...)` was ever reached. Fixed by introducing a `claimed` local + `break`.
The gap: `tests/test_jobs_worker.py::test_dead_letter_is_reported_not_silent` covers only the WORKER path, and `test_dead_letter_signal_is_emitted_by_the_reaper_too` only the REAPER path. Neither exercises `claim_next`'s claim-and-settle-in-one-call shape — which is exactly why this shipped green. jobs-queue notes that shape is the COMMON one (a worker polling a backlog routinely settles a spent job and claims the next unit in the same pass), so the signal was lost nearly every time it mattered.
Required case: `max_attempts=1`; enqueue A then B; spend A's attempt; requeue A as pending with budget spent; call `claim_next()` ONCE. Assert a `validsim_job_dead_lettered` record IS emitted for A (reason retry-budget-exhausted) AND B is claimed in the same call. The pre-fix control is that the same setup with ONLY A (no B) did signal — so also keep/assert that case so the test pins the asymmetry, not just the happy path.

# Repro table for the `notify/config.py` index-alignment fix

Source of truth: `d:/SIM-TO-REAL/validsim/notify/config.py`. `_split_positional()` (config.py:180-196) replaces the blank-dropping `_split()` for the three index-paired companions. `_split()` is still used for `VALIDSIM_WEBHOOK_URLS` (a blank there is padding, not a destination).

These are the exact cases. Env dict passed to `notify_config_from_env()` is shown as `KEY=value` pairs; every other key is absent.

## A. The defect class — blank placeholder must hold position

| # | `VALIDSIM_WEBHOOK_URLS` | `VALIDSIM_WEBHOOK_SECRETS` | expected `[hook.secret, ...]` | before fix (buggy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `https://a/h,https://b/h` | `,s2` | `[None, "s2"]` | `["s2", None]` ❌ |
| 2 | `https://a/h,https://b/h,https://c/h` | `,s2,s3` | `[None, "s2", "s3"]` | `["s2", "s3", None]` ❌ |
| 3 | `https://a/h,https://b/h` | `s1,` | `["s1", None]` | `["s1", None]` (unchanged) |
| 4 | `https://a/h,https://b/h` | `,` | `[None, None]` | `[None, None]` (unchanged) |

Case 1 is the money shot: hook 1 was signed with hook 2's key and hook 2 was left unsigned — the exact inverse of intent. Case 2 shows it cascades.

## B. Same defect via the other two companions

| `VALIDSIM_WEBHOOK_URLS` | companion | expected | before (buggy) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `https://a/h,https://b/h` | `VALIDSIM_WEBHOOK_FORMATS=,slack` | `[json, slack]` | `[slack, json]` ❌ |
| `https://a/h,https://b/h` | `VALIDSIM_WEBHOOK_MIN_SEVERITY=,warn` | `[info, warn]` | `[warn, info]` ❌ |

The severity one matters operationally: `,warn` silently demoted hook 1 to `warn` while hook 2 kept `info` — an inverted routing table where the hook the operator meant to make loud stayed quiet on info events.

## C. Behaviours that must NOT regress (all currently pass)

| # | Input | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `URLS=a,b` + `SECRETS=s1` (genuinely shorter) | `["s1", None]` |
| 2 | `URLS=a,b` + `SECRETS=s1,s2` (full pairing) | `["s1", "s2"]` |
| 3 | `URLS=a` + `SECRETS=` absent/empty | `[None]` |
| 4 | `URLS=a` + `FORMATS=xml` | `[json]` (invalid format falls back) |
| 5 | `URLS=a` + `MIN_SEVERITY=loud` | `[info]` (invalid severity falls back) |
| 6 | `URLS=not-a-url,https://b/h` + `SECRETS=s1,s2` | one hook, secret `"s2"` (malformed URL dropped, survivor keeps `s2` because it was at index 1) |
| 7 | `URLS=a,b,c`, no companions | hook names `[webhook-1, webhook-2, webhook-3]` |

## Two things worth encoding deliberately

1. **Case C6 is the documented sharp edge, not a bug.** Dropping a *URL* still re-indexes survivors, so a companion list must be kept in original positions. My docstring now states this. If you write a test for C6, please pin the *current* behaviour with a comment noting it is a known sharp edge — I don't want a future reader to "fix" it as if it were the same class of defect.
2. **Case 4/5 fallback interacts with blanks.** `URLS=a,b` + `FORMATS=,xml` → hook 1 `json` (blank), hook 2 `json` (invalid → default). Both end up `json`, so this case does not distinguish pass/fail — don't use it as the regression guard for B; use the valid-sibling version (`FORMATS=,slack`) which does.

Current status: **435 passed / 1 failed** on my subset. The single failure is `test_notify_ssrf_timeout_agent.py::test_delivery_is_blind_so_the_response_cannot_be_relayed`, asserting `set(vars(result)) == {"name","url","ok","status_code","error"}` — `'dry_run'` is the only extra key. team-lead has asked you to own that assertion update; the field is `dry_run: bool`, default `False`, meaning "recorded without any network I/O", mirroring `EmailDelivery.dry_run`. Note that test's *other* assertions (loopback SSRF reachability, response body never relayed) still pass — the security property is intact.

I have not written or edited any test. Tell me if you want the repro table in a different shape.

Both items are ON DISK and verified by execution. Nothing speculative — you can write both tests now.

## 1) `_split_positional()` repro table

I ran every case through the real `notify_config_from_env()`. Your four cases match my verified values exactly. Two things your assumptions need pinning:

**Your question "shorter companion list pads with a safe default vs `None`":** the answer is **`None`, not a safe default**. A genuinely shorter list produces `None` because `_at()` returns `None` and `HookSpec` declares `secret: str | None`. There is no `"info"`/`"json"` substitution at this layer — `"info"` is the `min_severity` *field default*, which every hook gets regardless. Don't assert a safe-default sentinel for the secret; assert `None`.

**On hook naming — important, and the opposite of what my earlier note implied:** names derive from the URL's position in the **raw** env string, i.e. `webhook-{index+1}` over the loop index of `_split(URLS)`, *before* any dropping. Verified: `URLS=not-a-url,https://b.example/h` yields **one** hook named **`webhook-2`**, not `webhook-1`. So name and secret are *both* positional on the raw index. Please pin that explicitly — it's what makes case C3 coherent.

### Verified table (executed, not transcribed)

URLs used: `https://a.example/h,https://b.example/h,https://c.example/h` (truncated per row).

| case | `SECRETS` | verified hooks `(name, secret, format, min_severity)` |
|---|---|---|
| A1 blank placeholder hook 1 | `,s2` | `(webhook-1, None, json, info)`, `(webhook-2, "s2", json, info)` |
| A2 blank placeholder hook 1 of 3 | `,s2,s3` | `(webhook-1, None, …)`, `(webhook-2, "s2", …)`, `(webhook-3, "s3", …)` |
| A3 trailing blank | `s1,` | `(webhook-1, "s1", …)`, `(webhook-2, None, …)` |
| A4 all blank | `,` | `(webhook-1, None, …)`, `(webhook-2, None, …)` |
| A5 genuinely shorter | `s1` | `(webhook-1, "s1", …)`, `(webhook-2, None, …)` |
| A6 full pairing | `s1,s2` | `(webhook-1, "s1", …)`, `(webhook-2, "s2", …)` |
| A7 absent entirely | *(unset)* | `(webhook-1, None, …)`, `(webhook-2, None, …)` |

A3/A4/A5/A7 are the **no-regression** rows — identical before and after my fix. A1/A2 are the actual bug.

### B. Same defect via the other two companions

| case | companion | verified |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | `VALIDSIM_WEBHOOK_FORMATS=,slack` | `(webhook-1, json, info)`, `(webhook-2, slack, info)` |
| B2 | `VALIDSIM_WEBHOOK_MIN_SEVERITY=,warn` | `(webhook-1, info)`, `(webhook-2, warn)` |

B2 is the one with operational teeth: before the fix hook 1 became `warn` and hook 2 stayed `info` — an inverted routing table.

### C. Other must-not-regress

| case | input | verified |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | `URLS=https://a.example/h` + `FORMATS=xml` | `(webhook-1, json, info)` |
| C2 | `URLS=…a…` + `MIN_SEVERITY=loud` | `(webhook-1, json, info)` |
| C3 | `URLS=not-a-url,https://b.example/h` + `SECRETS=s1,s2` | **one** hook `(webhook-2, "s2", …)` |
| C4 | `URLS=a,b,c`, no companions | names `[webhook-1, webhook-2, webhook-3]` |

**Please pin C3 with a comment marking it a known sharp edge, not a bug.** Dropping a *URL* still re-indexes survivors; that's intentional (one bad destination must not disable the others) and my `config.py` docstring now documents it. If C3 is written as a plain "must not regress" row it will read like an accident and invite a future "fix" that breaks the drop-a-bad-URL behaviour.

**One trap:** `URLS=a,b` + `FORMATS=,xml` is a *bad* guard — both hooks end up `json`, so it passes both pre- and post-fix. Use B1's valid-sibling form instead.

## 2) `DeliveryResult.dry_run` — all four answers, field is live

- **Exact attribute name:** `dry_run`
- **Dataclass field or property?** **Dataclass field** → it **does** appear in `vars()`. Your line 314 edit is therefore a **set addition only**:
  `{"name", "url", "ok", "status_code", "error", "dry_run"}`
  No value change is needed to that specific assertion.
- **Type:** `bool`

- **Semantics — you asked which polarity:** `dry_run=True` means **"this was a dry run"** (recorded, nothing left the process). `dry_run=False` means a real network attempt was made. So the flag reads as "this is a rehearsal", i.e. `dry_run` is *true when nothing was sent* — the opposite polarity to "delivered for real".

  Exact values, verified against real sockets (not mocks):
  - dry-run dispatch → `(ok=True, status_code=None, dry_run=True, error=None)`
  - live success, real 200 → `(ok=True, status_code=200, dry_run=False, error=None)`
  - live failure, connection refused → `(ok=False, status_code=None, dry_run=False, error=<transport error>)`

  Note the third row: it is `(ok=False, status_code=None)`, which was **indistinguishable from the dry-run row** before this field existed. That collision is the reason for the field. If you want to pin it, the connection-refused case is the one worth asserting.

- **Default:** `False`. I set it **explicitly at all three** construction sites (dry-run branch → `True`; both `_post()` sites → `False`), so every in-repo construction is explicit rather than default-dependent.

- **Field order (matters only if you assert a tuple):** `['name', 'url', 'ok', 'status_code', 'error', 'dry_run']` — `dry_run` is **last**, so append it at the end of your set literal, not after `ok`.

- **Backwards-compat note for your own test:** constructing positionally and omitting it yields `dry_run=False`, which is the correct fail-safe direction (default to "this really happened", not "this was a rehearsal"). If you have a helper that builds `DeliveryResult` positionally, it will keep working unchanged.

One thing I'd ask you to cover if you have room: a **cross-notifier consistency** assertion that `EmailDelivery.dry_run` and `DeliveryResult.dry_run` share the same polarity and default — that's the invariant my docstring claims, and right now nothing pins it.

`tests/test_wiring_reachability_agent.py::test_allow_listed_capability_is_genuinely_unwired` fails for 3 params. Cause: `api-surface` legitimately wired three capabilities into production, but the `UNWIRED_BY_DESIGN` allow-list at lines 251-261 is now stale. Current entries:
  line 251: ("validsim.api.store_stats", "store_totals"): "O(1) store summary; no production caller yet"
  line 252: ("validsim.api.store_stats", "run_summaries"): "O(1) run summaries; no production caller yet"
  lines 253-256: ("validsim.api.store_stats", "latest_composite"): "O(1) latest composite; no production caller yet"
  lines 257-260: ("validsim.api.store_stats", "strategy_for"): "pick query strategy; only called by the unwired store_stats readers"
  line 261: ("validsim.api.store_stats", "StoreTotals"): "result type of the unwired store_totals"

FIX: remove exactly THREE keys — `store_totals`, `latest_composite`, `StoreTotals` — and update their reason strings to say they are now wired via `metrics._summary`.
CRITICAL: DO NOT remove `run_summaries` or `strategy_for`. Both are STILL genuinely unwired and the guard is correct about them. api-surface explicitly confirmed it did NOT wire them and deliberately deferred that as a follow-up. Removing them would silently destroy a real safety guard.
Also note the stale reason on `strategy_for` references "the unwired store_stats readers" — once `store_totals` is wired, reword it minimally so it is not self-contradictory, but keep the key.
This test is doing its job. It is a capability-reachability guard, and api-surface changed a capability's reachability. Removing the three stale entries is the correct fix, not weakening the guard.

=== TASK #3 — correction to a spec I gave you (IMPORTANT, do this before writing the site test) ===
`site-astro` self-corrected and I need to correct MY mistake to you. I told you the site's `72.7` figure was underived and to treat it as suspect.
